name: kalindudc
description: bb plugins by Kalindu De Costa.

categories.description: Change what people see or do inside an open thread.
Change how threads are listed and organized in the sidebar.
Create and manage where threads run, locally or in the cloud.
Plan, track, route, schedule, or automate work.
Personalize how bb looks and feels.
Small tools that make everyday work in bb smoother, such as keeping plugins up to date.

plugins.description: Run your own prompt files from ~/.agents/commands in any bb thread. Type ! for a menu of them, or type /name as you would in pi: codex and Claude Code agents learn to run it, and pi expands it itself.
plugins.overview:
Use your own slash-command prompts from `~/.agents/commands` in any bb thread, whichever agent runs it.

## What you get

- Type `!` in a composer to open a Commands menu listing every `.md` file in `~/.agents/commands`, with its description and argument hint. The list is read fresh from disk as you type, so a new or edited file shows up straight away.
- Pick a command, type its arguments after it, and send. The plugin attaches the command's instructions to your message for the agent, and you see only the pill and your arguments in the thread.
- Type `/name arguments` as plain text and it works too. Codex and Claude Code agents are told which commands exist and to run `/name` from the folder. pi expands `/name` itself when `~/.pi/agent/prompts` links to `~/.agents/commands`, so the plugin adds nothing to pi threads in that case.

## The command files

Each command is one Markdown file in pi's prompt template format. The file name is the command name, `description` and `argument-hint` come from the frontmatter, and the body can use `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1` and `${@:2}` for the arguments:

```markdown
---
description: Review staged git changes
argument-hint: "[focus]"
---
Review the staged changes. Focus on ${1:-correctness}.
```

To keep pi on the same files, make its prompts folder a link: `ln -s ../../.agents/commands ~/.pi/agent/prompts`.

## Limits

- bb's `/` menu is fed by skills and the agent's own command folders, and plugins cannot add to it, so the menu uses `!`.
- A `!` command attaches its text when you send, before bb knows the message, so the placeholders are not filled in. The agent is told that the rest of your message is the arguments and how `$ARGUMENTS`, `$1` and `${@:N}` map onto it.
- Typed `/name` has been tested in pi and codex threads. The `!` menu does not depend on the agent, because bb attaches the command text itself.
- The menu reads the folder on the machine that runs the bb server. Typed `/name` commands are read by the agent on the thread's own machine.
- Only top-level `.md` files with names made of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` are listed, like pi.

plugins.description: Makes bb's Browser follow your real browser. Sessions from the Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi or Firefox profile you pick flow into bb while that browser stays open, on macOS and Linux; sign-in pages such as Okta, Google and Microsoft are handed to your real browser where passkeys and Okta Verify work, and Cmd+click (Ctrl+click) opens a link in your real browser.
plugins.overview:
Make bb's Browser follow the browser you already use, so you stop re-importing cookies and closing your browser every time a session expires.

## What you get

- **Sessions that keep up.** Pick a browser and profile once. Whenever that browser saves its cookies, the ones that changed are copied into bb's Browser while the browser stays open. Signing in or out in your browser carries over to bb within about 30 seconds, which is how often Chromium browsers write cookies to disk.
- **Sign-in finishes in your real browser.** When a bb Browser tab stops on an Okta, Microsoft, Google, Auth0, OneLogin, Duo, Ping or GitHub sign-in form, the plugin first copies your browser's current session and reloads the tab; that is enough when your browser is already signed in. If the form is still there, the page opens in your browser, where passkeys, Touch ID, security keys and Okta Verify work. bb reloads the tab once the new session arrives. Add your own sign-in pages in the settings, or switch the handoff to a button or off.
- **Cmd+click opens links in your browser.** Cmd+click on macOS (Ctrl+click elsewhere) opens a link in the browser you picked, in the same profile, instead of a new bb tab.
- **A sync button.** Beside the address bar, a button syncs sessions now, with the last sync or any problem in its tooltip.
- **`bb better-browser`** prints the status, lists browsers and profiles, syncs, and opens a link, for you or an agent.

## Browsers

Sessions sync from Google Chrome, Chromium, Arc, Dia, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Helium, Firefox and Zen on macOS, and from Google Chrome, Chromium, Brave, Microsoft Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Firefox and Zen on Linux. Safari can open links, but its sessions do not sync yet.

## How it works

The plugin runs on the computer with the bb app. It reads a private copy of the profile's cookie database, so the browser can stay open, and decrypts Chromium cookies with the browser's "Safe Storage" key. On macOS the first sync shows a Keychain prompt; choose Always Allow. On Linux the secret comes from the Secret Service or KWallet, falling back to the basic password store, and cookies that none of those can decrypt are reported as unreadable. It writes cookies into bb's Browser through a hidden tab it borrows for a moment and closes again.

Only cookies that changed in your browser since the last sync are written. A cookie a site changed inside bb is never overwritten with an older copy, and a cookie your browser dropped is removed from bb only while bb still holds the copy the plugin wrote. Cookie values never leave your computer; the plugin stores only hashes of what it synced.

## Limits

- bb's Browser is still bb's own engine, so a page that needs a passkey or Okta Verify cannot use them inside bb; the handoff sends that step to your browser instead.
- Partitioned (CHIPS) cookies and cookies a browser binds to the device are not copied, like bb's own import.
- Session sync needs the bb desktop app, and a sync runs only while a bb Browser tab is open.

plugins.description: Expands thinking blocks in threads automatically and keeps streaming thinking scrolled into view. Toggle it from the thread header or a thread's actions menu.
plugins.overview:
Watch an agent reason without clicking each thinking row open and scrolling inside it while the text streams.

## What you get

- The live **Thinking…** row at the bottom of a running thread opens by itself and stays scrolled to its newest line.
- Finished **Thought** rows open when they appear, including the ones inside an activity group once you open that group.
- Scroll up inside a thinking block to read earlier text and it stops following; scroll back to the bottom and it follows again.
- A block you collapse stays collapsed.
- A brain button in the thread header turns the plugin on or off, and so do the **Follow thinking** item in any thread's actions menu (the one phones use, since their header leaves the button out) and the command **Follow Thinking: Toggle auto-expand and auto-scroll of thinking** in the command palette. Turning it off collapses the blocks it opened and leaves the ones you opened.

## How it works

The plugin runs in the bb window and works on the timeline bb already draws. It needs no account, settings or server state. The on/off choice is saved on each device and shared by every bb window there.

## Limits

bb has no plugin interface for timeline rows, so the plugin recognises thinking blocks by the markup that bb 0.46 draws. If a bb update changes that markup, the plugin stops doing anything until it is updated; the timeline itself keeps working.

plugins.description: Six web-research tools for every BB agent: search, fetch, map, deterministic extraction, bounded crawl jobs and snapshot diffs. Durable scoped sources, Sources UI, zero-turn CLI and privacy ceilings share one runtime.
plugins.overview:
Forage gives every BB agent six web-research tools, durable scoped evidence and a CLI that uses no model turns. Requires BB 0.47 or newer.

## Research tools

- `web_search`: up to eight queries, domain/date filters, provider profiles and fair host-diverse content reads.
- `web_fetch`: up to ten URLs, readable or exact textual raw mode, independent direct/GitHub-smart resolution, passage search and outline/link/line/focus views.
- `web_map`: bounded sitemap, robots, llms.txt and HTML discovery with provenance.
- `web_extract`: deterministic metadata, headings, links, tables and JSON-LD. No hidden AI extraction.
- `web_crawl`: persistent start/status/list/cancel/resume jobs with page, depth, byte, time and concurrency limits.
- `web_diff`: immutable snapshot comparison or a fresh URL against stored evidence.

Content is captured before formatting. Continue with snapshotId, contentHash and UTF-16 offset for immutable paging. URL-only paging may download again after cache expiry. Every batch failure and partial limit is visible; output is capped at 32,000 characters.

## Sources

The project Sources page and thread tab preview evidence, show citations and diffs, manage jobs, copy public sources to the project, and export streamed NDJSON. IDs from another thread are invisible: share URLs or findings unless explicitly project-promoted.

Default retention is 30 days for thread content, 180 days for project content and 128 MiB retained content. Active-job snapshots are protected. Storage refusal never produces a fictional source ID. Missed deletion events are recovered using authoritative scope checks; archived threads are not deleted.

## Privacy and providers

Keyless DuckDuckGo and Exa work without credentials. Optional Brave, Exa account, SearXNG and Tavily search, explicit Tavily/Firecrawl/Jina readers, and an explicit Firecrawl crawl backend respect configured ceilings. Keys do not automatically enable paid fallback.

Profiles: auto, fast, fresh, docs, private and deep. Private allows configured SearXNG search, direct readers and local crawl only; it makes no guarantee about SearXNG's upstream engines. Per-call arguments cannot widen setting-level privacy.

Private networks are blocked by default and each direct redirect is revalidated and DNS-pinned. Local private-network permission is not permission to forward URLs to a cloud reader. Remote URLs are screened before forwarding; vendor-side redirects cannot be DNS-pinned locally.

Restricted same-thread capture is OFF by default, cannot be project-promoted, and needs explicit thread selection for export. Disabling it revokes reads. Credentials/headers/cookies are never persisted. Sensitive URL checks are conservative heuristics, not a general secret detector. Scope isolation does not protect SQLite from a local user or shell-capable agent.

## CLI and diagnostics

`bb forage search|fetch|map|extract|diff` and `crawl start|status|list|cancel|resume` take explicit --project/--thread IDs and strict --input JSON. Tools and CLI share one runtime, repository, job service and diagnostic ring.

Sources commands: list, show, export, delete and prune. Destructive commands require exact confirmation tokens; export returns a local-auth download route, not a server file path.

`status` and `diagnostics` show redacted in-memory records (maximum 200, 24 hours), never query/URL/content/credential values. `clear` clears process caches. `doctor` is offline unless --live explicitly enables bounded keyless probes. `bench` runs a bundled local corpus without network access.

See the README and bundled research skill for parameters, limits and safe continuation.

plugins.description: A gruvbox theme for coding: 0px corners, flat surfaces, a JetBrains Mono interface and a composer styled as a terminal prompt, so bb reads like a terminal. Dark mode is gruvbox soft (#32302f); light mode keeps gruvbox's ink on a neutral paper base instead of the yellow #fbf1c7, with accents darkened to stay readable. Ships gruvbox syntax colours for diffs and a gruvbox terminal palette for each mode. Pick Gruve under Settings → Appearance.
plugins.overview:
A gruvbox theme for bb, tuned for long coding sessions: sharp corners, flat surfaces and a monospace UI, so bb reads like a terminal.

## What you get

- Dark mode is gruvbox soft: a `#32302f` canvas and a `#2b2928` sidebar, one step lighter than stock gruvbox, with gruvbox yellow as the accent.
- Light mode keeps gruvbox's ink and accents but trades the yellow `#fbf1c7` background for a neutral paper `#f4f1e8`. Accents use gruvbox's darker faded shades so links and status text stay readable.
- 0px corners everywhere bb uses its radius scale, and no drop shadows. Avatars, spinners, status dots and pills stay round.
- JetBrains Mono for the whole interface, code and the integrated terminal. It falls back to your system monospace font when JetBrains Mono is not installed.
- A composer styled as a terminal prompt: a `❯` before your first line, a yellow caret, an accent border while it has focus, and an outlined send button.
- Gruvbox syntax colours in diffs and file previews: gruvbox dark soft and gruvbox light hard.
- A gruvbox terminal palette for each mode.

Every text colour clears 4.5:1 contrast on the canvas, cards, menus, sidebar and hovered rows in both modes, and so does every terminal colour except black. A test keeps it that way.

## Turn it on

Pick **Gruve** under **Settings → Appearance**, or run:

```sh
bb theme set plugin:gruve:gruve
```

Light or dark is still bb's own per-client setting.

## Limits

- It sets bb's theme tokens and styles bb's own composer, nothing else. Plugins that draw their own UI, such as a custom sidebar, keep their own corner radii and pick up the colours through bb's variables. If you choose another composer under Settings → Appearance → Composer, Gruve leaves it alone.
- The composer styling relies on bb's `data-promptbox` markup, so a bb release that changes it can drop the prompt glyph until Gruve is updated. The colours are unaffected.
- The integrated terminal paints on the sidebar colour, so it is paper in light mode rather than dark.

plugins.description: Open this bb from phones and laptops on your home network: pair a device once with a code or QR code, then use bb in its browser at <computer>.local, its LAN IP or your own name. No bb account or getbb.app needed.
plugins.overview:
Use this bb from your phone, tablet or another laptop on the same home network, in the device's browser. No bb account, no getbb.app and nothing to install on the device.

## What you get

- A "LAN access" switch. When it is on, bb answers on port 38890 on your local network, at its LAN IP address (such as `http://192.168.1.20:38890`), at any name you add yourself, and at the computer's Bonjour name (such as `http://macbook-pro.local:38890`).
- A settings section, on the plugin's page and on bb's Mobile settings page, that shows the URLs, pairs new devices with a QR code and lists paired devices with buttons to turn each one off and on, or revoke it.
- `bb lan status`, `on`, `off`, `pair`, `devices`, `enable`, `disable` and `revoke` in the terminal, so agents and scripts can do the same.
- The full bb app on the device: threads stream live, and terminals work.

## Pairing

Press "Pair a device" or run `bb lan pair`. You get a QR code, a link and an eight-character code. The link uses your first extra hostname, or the LAN IP address when you have none, because many phones cannot resolve `.local` names. Scan the code or open the link on the device and press "Pair this device". The code works once and expires after five minutes. The device then stays paired for 400 days, or until you revoke it.

To block a device for a while, turn it off in the device list or with `bb lan disable <id>`. It keeps its pairing and sees a "LAN access is off" page until you turn it back on, so you can switch a machine's access on and off without pairing it again. Turning a device off or revoking it closes its open connection at once. A device pairs once for each name it uses, so use one name per device.

## Names you can use

- The LAN IP addresses, listed in the status. Give the computer a fixed address in your router (a DHCP reservation): a device pairs per address, so a new address means pairing again.
- The computer's `.local` name, which Macs and most Linux machines announce on the network by themselves. Macs and iPhones resolve it; many Android phones and some Wi-Fi networks do not.
- Your own name, such as `bb.home.arpa`: add a DNS record for it in your router or Pi-hole that points at this computer, then add it under "Extra hostnames".
- On macOS you can set the port to 80 to drop the port from the URL.

## Security

- Only devices with private-network addresses are answered, and only for the names above. Tailscale addresses are refused.
- Devices that have not paired never reach bb. They see the pairing page.
- A paired device can do everything you can do in bb, including running commands in terminals. Pair only your own devices, and revoke one you lose.
- Requests that another website starts in a paired browser are refused, except plain links that open the app.
- Without HTTPS, traffic and the device cookie travel unencrypted, and browsers block voice input and clipboard access. To serve HTTPS, make a certificate (for example with mkcert, and install its root certificate on each device) and set the certificate and key file settings.

## Not included

- The native bb mobile app pairs only through getbb.app, so it cannot use LAN Connect. Use the phone's browser.
- Sharing agents' dev-server ports, and publishing extra `.local` names.

plugins.description: Hand a goal to agents and keep the decisions. A planner turns it into a spec with tickets, acceptance criteria, checks and a merge plan, and a separate agent reviews the spec before you approve it. Workers then build each ticket in its own git worktree, Loom runs your checks, and reviewers on another model approve the work or send findings back. Approved work merges into an integration branch you land as one pull request, or opens as one pull request per ticket that Loom follows through CI. A full-screen Loom page shows what each project is for, what needs you, the board, every attempt and review, the order to merge stacked pull requests in, the changes before they land, insights on how the project went and a timeline you can rewind.
plugins.overview:
Run a software project with agents. A planner turns your goal into a spec and a ticket board, workers build each ticket in its own git worktree, separate reviewers approve the work or send it back, and approved work merges into an integration branch or opens as pull requests. You follow and steer it from the Loom page in bb's left navigation, or with `bb loom`.

## What you get

- Planning from any thread with the `loom-plan` skill, or from New project on the Loom page. The planner asks its questions (Ask User Question rounds, one question at a time on its page) and proposes a spec: tickets with acceptance criteria, check commands, a review policy and a merge plan.
- A spec review before you see it: a separate agent checks the spec against your request and for work the goal does not need.
- Spec review without reading TOML: how it runs, the tickets by wave and the goal, opening on what changed since the last version. Click any part to comment on it or suggest a value ("+ note" on files), and the planner gets every comment in one message.
- Workers that start by themselves, one per ready ticket in its own worktree, once its dependencies are done and its files clear the work in flight. Loom, not the agent, commits, runs your checks and decides whether the work passed.
- Reviewers on their own model that approve or send numbered findings back. A ticket merges only after the review you asked for and the `after_merge` checks on the merged result.
- Two ways to ship: an integration branch you read on the Changes tab and land as one pull request, or straight onto the base with `--direct`; or one pull request per ticket that the worker writes and Loom follows through CI and review. A dependent ticket stacks on its dependency's open pull request instead of waiting for the merge, and a worker frees its environment while its pull request waits.
- Deploy order as advice: a Rollout tab and a section in each pull request show the next safe step and what must be live first.
- Projects across repos: list bb projects as `[[repo]]` tables, and each ticket runs in one, with that repo's checks and integration branch.
- A Loom page: a home table that puts what needs you first, a next-step bar with the one button you need now, a board with a row per stage, a ticket page with every attempt, check, review and merge, an Agents tab, and an Insights tab that says how the project went, when its work happened and what happened to each ticket, with the numbers beside the story.
- A timeline on every project: rewind the page to any moment or play it back.
- Blocked tickets go to the planner in a triage round, and your reply on one reaches it at once. The Loom icon in the navigation rail counts what needs you, and the Loom page swaps bb's sidebar for its projects and the open project's tickets.
- `bb loom metrics`, `feed` and `report` print the numbers, the events and a finished project's record. A done hook sends that record, or an agent's summary of it, to a command you choose.

## How it works

Every change appends an event, in the same transaction, to a log that refuses edits, so metrics from it are exact. Agents get narrow tools for their role and never merge or push. On the integration strategy the branch stays local until you land it; on the pull request strategy Loom pushes the reviewed work, never with force, and you merge. A worker's pull request comments come from your account, so each ends with a signature line, "Posted by Loom" unless you change it in Loom's settings. Every button that changes something asks for a second click and is logged as your action.

## Requirements

- `git` on the machine that has the project's checkouts.
- `gh`, signed in, for GitHub pull requests; for another server, the commands you set in the spec's `[merge.forge]`.
- Provider usage: every planner, worker and reviewer is an ordinary bb thread, so your providers' limits apply. A token budget or a deadline in the spec has Loom pause the project for you.

plugins.description: Let your own pi setup write bb's thread titles and commit messages: your credentials and model, no bb account needed. Adds a one-click regenerate-title button to the thread header and its actions menu, plus pi executable and model knobs in the plugin settings.
plugins.overview:
Delegate bb's helper AI tasks to the pi CLI on your machine.

## What you get

- bb's thread titles and commit messages generated by your own pi setup: your credentials, your model, your defaults — no bb account or separate API key needed.
- A Model knob and a Pi executable knob under Settings → Installed plugins → Pi AI Services (also editable with `bb plugin config pi-services`).
- A refresh button in the thread header that regenerates the current thread's title on demand, and the same action as **Regenerate title with pi** in every thread's actions menu. Phones get only the menu item, to keep their header uncluttered.

## How it works

The plugin registers a bb AI service that runs `pi --print --no-session --no-tools` on the machine that runs the bb server, optionally passing `--model` from the settings. bb calls it for thread titles and commit messages and cleans up the reply itself. The regenerate button and menu item call the plugin's own RPC, which asks pi for a fresh title and renames the thread.

Select the service under Settings → AI services, or run:

```sh
bb settings ai-services set thread-title pi
bb settings ai-services set commit-message pi
```

Automatic picks Pi CLI when bb cloud is not signed in.

## Limits

Text only: voice transcription is not provided. The pi CLI must be installed and signed in on the machine that runs the bb server; the plugin launches it as a one-shot process, so every call pays pi's startup cost. pi's tools are disabled (`--no-tools`) because bb asks for plain-text replies, and bb aborts text services after five seconds.

plugins.description: Gives a thread a title when bb's automatic title fails or times out, using the same Shopify AI model. `bb retitle <thread>` titles any thread again, and `bb retitle --untitled` backfills threads bb left untitled.
plugins.overview:
Titles the threads that bb's automatic titling leaves untitled.

bb asks its AI service for a title once, when a thread starts, and gives up if the answer takes more than 8 seconds. The thread then keeps the first 80 characters of your message as its name. Retitle notices and titles it with the Shopify AI proxy.

## What you get

- Automatic retry: about 10 seconds after a thread starts running, Retitle titles it if it is still untitled. Threads you renamed, hidden threads and prompts under five words (which bb leaves untitled on purpose) are left alone.
- `bb retitle <thread>` titles one thread again, even one that already has a title. Run inside a thread, `bb retitle` titles that thread.
- `bb retitle --untitled` backfills the newest 20 untitled, unarchived threads. Add `--limit <n>`, `--project <id>`, `--dry-run` to list them first, or `--json`.

## Better titles for command prompts

bb titles from everything in the first message, including the instructions a `!command` mention attaches out of your sight, such as the whole body of `~/.agents/commands/plan.md`. Retitle reads only what you typed and tells the model which commands you invoked, so a `!plan` thread is titled after the work, not the planner instructions.

## How it works

Retitle uses bb's own title prompt and the title model chosen in the Shopify AI plugin's settings (`bb plugin config shopify-ai`), and falls back to GLM 5.3 Flash when that plugin is missing or its model is not a chat-completions model. The proxy token comes from `SHOPIFY_PROXY_KEY` or `devx llm-gateway print-token --key` on the machine that runs the bb server.

## Limits

- Shopify only: it needs access to the Shopify AI proxy.
- Threads that start while the plugin is not loaded are not retried; run `bb retitle --untitled` to catch them.
- The automatic retry runs once per thread per bb server run.

plugins.description: Check what an agent actually ran, changed and decided, in one live log beside the chat. Messages, thinking, commands with their output and exit codes, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps appear in timeline order, with a timestamp on every row and a duration on every command. It also shows what bb gives the agent but keeps out of the chat, such as plugin steers and mention context, marked Hidden. The log follows new output as it arrives, opens failed commands by default, and filters to messages, thinking, tools, hidden input or errors. Search covers the whole session and highlights every match, and single keys jump between rows, replies, errors and matches. Open it with Mod+Shift+L or from the thread header; it reads bb's timeline and keeps no copy of the thread.
plugins.overview:
See everything an agent did in a thread without opening nested chat rows.

## What you get

- One flat side-panel log in bb's timeline order: your messages and steers, child reports, agent replies, thinking, commands, tool calls, file diffs and subagent steps.
- What bb gives the agent but keeps out of the chat, marked Hidden where the agent received it: a plugin's steer, the context a mention resolves to, an automatic retry or a suppressed tool result.
- Rows tinted by type in your bb theme's colors, so replies, tool calls, commands, file changes and failures stand apart.
- Timestamps, status, exit codes and duration beside each step. Replies appear in full, long output previews its first and last lines, failed commands and tools open by default, and `x` expands every row.
- Filters for Messages, Thinking, Tools, Hidden and Errors, plus whole-session search that paints every match in amber and the current one in orange, with a counter and next/previous arrows (Enter and Shift+Enter in the search box). The log follows new output, including outputs that open up as they finish, until you scroll up or move to an older row; “↓ Latest” or `G` takes you back.
- Keyboard navigation (`j/k`, `n/N` for replies, or for matches while searching, `e/E` for errors), copy (`c`), a message link back to chat (`s`), and Mod+Shift+L to open the tab. The thread header has an open button too, except on phones, where the right panel's tab list opens the log. bb's Maximize pane button gives the log the whole window.
- Settings for preview sizes, whether failures open by themselves, which rows show when the log opens (hidden messages included), a 12- or 24-hour clock, and whether rows are tinted by type. Changes reach open panels straight away.

## How it works

The plugin loads bb's public timeline API, including nested rows, when you open the tab. It applies live deltas afterward, with at most two refresh requests a second. Because the timeline leaves hidden input out, it also reads the thread's request events and places each hidden message by its sequence number. It does not change bb's chat markup or store thread data; only the expanded-view choice is saved on this device. If you also want bb's chat itself to stop folding finished turns, use `bb settings completed-turns <provider> flat`.

## Limits

bb truncates output above 32,000 characters and the log keeps its truncation note. A match inside an expanded file diff is not painted, because bb's diff viewer keeps its own styles; stepping still frames its row. The whole session is fetched on opening, including large threads.

plugins.description: Your PRs and reviews across servers, saved PR boards, and agents that handle feedback, in one place.
plugins.overview:
See what each PR is waiting on and act without leaving bb. GitHub works out of the box; Delta, GitLab and other servers use command adapters.

## Five areas

- **Inbox:** the decisions waiting on you. Each PR says why it is here, what happens next and which action clears it. Snooze hides it until tomorrow or new activity.
- **My PRs:** your open PRs grouped by their next step or shown in a sortable list, followed by merged and closed PRs. Checks, reviews and agents stay beside each PR.
- **Reviews:** requests from people and teams, mentions and tracked PRs, grouped by where your review stands. Filter by team or hide bots and quiet PRs.
- **Boards:** saved PR sets for a release, project or handoff, across repositories and servers.
- **Insights:** review and merge times, feedback handled by agents, AI review results and the automation log. Sync shows each server's recent runs and explains failed steps.

## Saved PR boards

Create a board or save selected PRs from a list. Add members by searching Shuttle or pasting links and keys, filter the set, duplicate it, or remove members with confirmation and Undo. A PR can belong to several boards. Status stays live; merged and closed PRs remain until removed.

Archive a board without losing its PRs, then restore it before editing membership. Boards uses the same navigation as the other areas. Its compact timestamped activity log folds to its heading, with a remembered choice for each board on this device. Board membership never assigns agents or changes review tracking or feedback delivery.

## Work with agents

A PR's agent thread gets new reviews, comments and failed checks. Choose Fix it, Just tell it or Off. Auto agent, off by default, can find the thread on your PR's branch. Threads report which feedback they fixed, replied to or declined.

Start reviews from presets for the skill, model and workspace, or enable auto review. Reviewers hand back a draft; choose its findings and verdict before posting. Finished review threads are archived and brought back for the next review.

## Act on PRs

Merge, comment, reply, resolve threads, request reviewers, manage labels and post reviews as yourself. A thread's Shuttle tab shows its PRs in full. Search cached PRs or paste a link to look one up. Layouts adapt to phones and narrow windows, and lists remember their scroll, sort, filters and folded sections.

## Setup and tools

GitHub uses your authenticated `gh` CLI. Configure other servers with commands that print JSON; a working Delta adapter is included. Settings cover servers, presets, automations, agents and TOML import/export.

Agents use `shuttle_link`, `shuttle_prs`, `shuttle_review_draft` and `shuttle_feedback_done` for PR work, and the six `shuttle_board*` tools for saved sets. `bb shuttle` offers the same operations from the command line.

plugins.description: See which agent threads failed, need you or are still running, grouped under your bb sections. Child threads nest under their parent across projects, and a collapsed parent still shows its most urgent child. A status-lanes view lists every awake thread under Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle. Drag threads to reorder, nest or move them between sections, and snooze a quiet family until tomorrow morning. Hover a row for the thread's model, context use, branch, uncommitted changes and pull request. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each bb client.
plugins.overview:
Keep parallel agent threads readable and make triage part of the sidebar.

## What you get

- Your bb sections as coloured groups, with Pinned first and unfiled Threads last. Children form a tree across projects and sections; their own state and a collapsed parent's urgent descendants remain visible at a glance.
- A title, project, section and branch filter, status chips, three densities and an in-list View options menu, with short hints on the controls. Choose Switchboard under Settings → Appearance → Sidebar in each bb client.
- An Archive toggle shows archived threads on a shelf at the end of the list, with Unarchive and older pages on demand.
- A status-lanes view groups every awake thread under its own Failed, Needs you, Running, Unread or Idle state, newest attention first. An optional Needs-you shelf repeats urgent threads at the top without duplicating bb shortcuts.
- Hover a thread for an info card: model, context use, branch, changes, pull request and, in the Briefing layout, its first prompt and latest reply.

## Organize and triage

Drag threads above, below or under another thread, or onto a section header. Alt+arrow keys move a focused thread; Alt-click and Shift-click select families for bulk moves, archive and snooze. Section menus rename, colour, sort and add threads, and can set a default project that the section's + button uses for new threads. New sections start as an empty name field in place, and nothing is created until you press Enter. By-hand, recent-activity and status sort modes apply per section or to Threads. Sorted roots cannot be manually reordered, but you can still nest threads or move them onto a sorted section's header.

Idle unpinned families fade after your chosen number of days (three by default). A section menu can archive only its stale roots after a confirmation that counts their children, with Undo. Snooze a quiet family until 09:00 tomorrow (or your chosen local hour); the Snoozed shelf shows when it wakes and has a Wake button. New attention or an urgent or running child wakes it early.

Palette commands focus the filter (Mod+Alt+F), jump to the next failed or waiting thread (Mod+Alt+J), switch views and create a section.

## Parent threads and limits

Making a thread a child tells its parent's agent; bb then sends the parent each finished child turn. Undo within two seconds sends nothing, and bb allows at most four levels. Switchboard leaves parents, sections, pins and archives in bb, while its plugin store holds order, colour, collapse, sort, default projects and snooze. Status lanes reorder by design; the list does not window rows.

plugins.description: Groups every plugin with a waiting update at the top of the Installed plugins page, with each one's changelog from its source and one-click Update or Update all.
plugins.overview:
bb marks a plugin with a waiting update on its own card, but the Installed page has no filter or grouping, so the updates are easy to miss among dozens of cards. Update Shelf adds one group to the top of that page instead of a separate view.

## What you get

- A **N plugins have updates** group above the Installed cards, listing every plugin with a waiting update and its installed and new version.
- **What's new** on each row: the sections of the plugin's CHANGELOG.md newer than the version you run, read from the new release on GitHub. When the changelog has no entry, it lists the commits that changed the plugin since your version, with a link to the full comparison on GitHub.
- **Update** on each row and **Update all** in the header (after one confirmation). Updates run through bb's own update queue, one at a time, with bb's compatibility checks and rollback.
- Progress you can follow: the header counts the updates done, and each row shows its place in bb's queue, what bb is doing with the seconds so far, then Updated, or the reason with a Retry when an update fails or is rolled back. bb updates one plugin at a time and watches each new version for 30 seconds, so each takes about a minute.

## How it works

The backend reads the update state bb already keeps for each plugin, and the source bb records for it. Changelogs are read with the GitHub CLI when it is installed and signed in, so private repositories work; otherwise it falls back to GitHub's public API. A changelog is read only when you open What's new, and kept until the update changes.

## Requirements

- Changelogs come from GitHub sources only. Plugins from npm, other git hosts or a local path still show in the group and update normally, but What's new explains it has nothing to read.
- Private repositories need the GitHub CLI (`gh`) signed in on the machine running bb.
- bb has no plugin slot on the Installed page, so the group is placed next to the page's plugin cards by their markup. If a bb release changes that markup, the group stops appearing until this plugin is updated; bb's own page keeps working.

plugins.description: See every worktree your parallel agents work in, review what each one changed, and send your comments back to the agent that made the change. A full-screen Vantage page lists every recent thread's worktrees in bb's sidebar, grouped by what needs doing in plain words (Waiting on you, Ready to review, Still working, Done), and opens the worktree that needs you first, showing its changes as a stream of diffs with a file tree, side-by-side view and expandable context, plus an overlaps page for files two worktrees both changed and an All changes view by repository. Inside a thread, a Vantage tab lists its child threads' worktrees, a folded summary above the composer names the ones that need you, and an Info section shows the counts. Every thread shows its real state and every file has a Reviewed tick, with nothing to turn on; two settings choose the badge and toasts for threads that need you.
plugins.overview:
See every worktree your parallel agents work in, review what each one changed, and send your comments back to the agent that made the change: on a full-screen page for every recent thread, or inside one thread.

## What you get

- A Vantage page in bb's left navigation. While it is open, its worktree list replaces bb's thread list: worktrees grouped by what needs doing (Waiting on you, Ready to review, Still working, Done, Unavailable, Archived) or by project, with search and filter chips. Each row is two lines: the thread and its line counts, then one plain sentence such as "The agent asked you a question" or "Shares README.md with Banner". bb's title bar says where you are.
- One worktree at a time, never a second index beside the list: the page opens the worktree that needs you first, then one switch for all, uncommitted, committed or one commit's changes, a file tree with folders that fold, and every diff in one stream, unified or side by side, with unchanged lines you can expand and long lines that can wrap (`W`). Collapse all and Expand all (or `X`) fold and open every file at once. Vantage remembers these choices, and what you fold, across reloads.
- Comments on files, optionally quoting selected lines. They collect into one message you preview, then send to the agent now or after its current turn. The agent's chat opens in the page's Agent tab.
- An overlaps page for files that two worktrees both changed, with a guess at whether merging will conflict and a ready-made "ask to rebase" comment.
- All changes: everything the threads changed, by repository, including checkouts agents edited by path, archived branches and files outside any repository.
- In a thread: a Vantage tab with the same list, review and All changes; a one-line summary above the composer that stays folded until you open it and shows only once a child thread has changes; a Worktrees section in the Info tab; and "Review changes in Vantage" in the thread menu.
- Each worktree shows its branch, how far it is behind its base, its uncommitted files and commits, its pull request (from bb's GitHub PR Status plugin), and a terminal and copy path for its folder.

## Nothing to turn on

- Every thread shows its real state, the one bb's sidebar shows: a thread waiting for your answer or with a failed turn is under Waiting on you.
- Every file has a Reviewed tick. A ticked file folds away, and a worktree shows its progress once you tick one of its files. A file that changes after you tick it shows as changed.
- Two settings choose the alerts: a badge on the Vantage icon counting threads that need you (on by default) and a toast when one starts waiting (off by default).

## For agents

`bb vantage worktrees` prints one line for each worktree, then the shared files. `bb vantage worktree <thread>` prints one thread's files and commits. `bb vantage changes` prints All changes. Each accepts `--json`; `--thread <id>` reads another thread, and `--all` (with `--hours <n>`) reads every recent thread, grouped by project, and `--archived` adds the archived ones.

## How it works

Vantage never stages, commits or changes a file. It keeps reviewed marks in its plugin storage, and comment drafts and view choices in the browser. Counts come from bb's status call; other checkouts are read with git on the machine that owns them. Results are kept for 60 seconds and reloaded where an agent's edit or a workspace change touched.

## Limits

- 500 files per list, 100 commits per worktree, patches cut at 1 MiB.
- Comments are per file, not per line. The conflict guess compares changed line ranges; it is not a real merge.
- A checkout outside bb gets its own row only after the thread has both edited a file in it and changed into it with `cd`, `pushd` or `git -C`.
